Retinoid and AHA: not on the same night
Both make skin turn over faster. Use them on alternate nights, or acid once or twice a week.
Retinoid and salicylic acid: alternate nights
Together they often cause peeling and stinging. A salicylic wash in the morning is a gentler way to keep both.
Don't peel while using a retinoid
Skip peels entirely, or pause the retinoid for a week before and after, ideally with a professional's advice.
Go easy on scrubs with a retinoid
Retinoid-treated skin is thinner on top and tears more easily. Swap the scrub for a soft cloth.
Benzoyl peroxide in the morning, retinoid at night
Benzoyl peroxide can break down tretinoin and retinol. Adapalene is stable with it, but splitting them still reduces dryness.
One exfoliating acid is usually enough
Using an AHA and a BHA daily is a common cause of over-exfoliation. Pick one, or alternate days.
Don't add a peel on top of daily acids
That's two exfoliating acids in one go. Stop the daily acid for a few days around a peel.

Vitamin C in the morning, acid at night
Both are acidic and can sting together. Splitting them keeps both working.

Keep vitamin C and benzoyl peroxide apart
Benzoyl peroxide breaks down vitamin C. Use one in the morning and the other at night, or BPO only as a rinse-off wash.
Vitamin C and niacinamide are fine together
The idea that they cancel each other out came from old lab tests with pure chemicals at high heat. In today's products they work well together.
Hydroquinone and benzoyl peroxide can stain
Together they can leave a temporary dark tint on skin. Use them at different times of day.
